title: Deepinder Goyal's Temple Doubles Valuation to $375 Million With Rare Early-Stage ESOP Buyback
excerpt: The Zomato founder's brain-monitoring wearable startup is letting employees cash in part of their stock at nearly double its seed-round price, with outside investors eyeing a $500 million valuation.
body:
• Temple, Deepinder Goyal's brain-monitoring wearable startup, has launched an ESOP buyback valuing the company at $375 million — nearly double its $190 million seed-round valuation from February.
  • Around 20 of Temple's 200-plus employees can sell up to 25% of their vested stock options; participation is voluntary.
  • External investors are circling at a $500 million valuation ahead of a planned funding round, making this one of the fastest valuation jumps for an early-stage Indian startup.
  • The startup is nearing commercial launch of its forehead-worn wearable that tracks cerebral blood flow in real time.

Five months after raising $54 million in a friends-and-family seed round, Deepinder Goyal's wearable technology startup Temple has nearly doubled in implied value and is giving early employees a chance to cash in before the next raise.

Temple has launched an ESOP liquidity programme that values the company at $375 million, according to an internal memo first reported by Moneycontrol. The buyback is open to roughly 20 of Temple's 200-to-220 employees, who can sell up to 25 percent of their vested stock options at that price. Participation is voluntary.

"We are seeing strong interest from external investors at a $500 million valuation. Before we close our next round, I want some of this value to reach the people who created it."

— Deepinder Goyal, Temple founder

An Unusual Move for a Pre-Revenue Startup

ESOP buybacks are rare at the early stage. Most startups wait until Series B or later, and even then the buyback price is typically at or below the last funding valuation. Temple is doing the opposite — pricing its buyback at nearly twice the seed round, while signalling that the next external round could value the company at $500 million.

https://x.com/chandrarsrikant/status/2081638973760516220

Inc42 reported that Temple declined to comment on the development. The startup raised its $54 million seed from Steadview Capital, Peak XV Partners, Vy Capital, and Info Edge, alongside founder-investors including Vijay Shekhar Sharma of Paytm, Kunal Shah of CRED, and Nithin and Nikhil Kamath of Zerodha. More than 30 employees had invested their own money at the same valuation, without a discount.

What Temple Is Building

Temple is developing a forehead-worn wearable designed to measure the body's metabolic state — specifically cerebral blood flow — in real time. The device grew out of Goyal's longevity-focused research initiative, Continue Research, which published a hypothesis suggesting that reduced blood flow to the brain caused by gravity could be an overlooked factor in human ageing.

The science has drawn both interest and scepticism from the medical community, but Goyal has maintained that even if the hypothesis does not hold, the wearable could succeed as a standalone consumer health device. Temple has partnered with Ethereal Machines and Zetwerk for manufacturing and is currently running an early-access programme ahead of a broader commercial launch.

Goyal's Post-Zomato Reinvention

Goyal stepped down as CEO of Zomato and its parent company Eternal in January, handing the role to Albinder Dhindsa, who leads the quick-commerce unit Blinkit. He remains vice chairman of Eternal. The move capped nearly two decades at the helm of the food delivery company he co-founded in 2008 and signalled a shift toward what Goyal called "higher-risk exploration and experimentation."

Regulatory filings show Goyal holds about 28 percent of Temple, while employees collectively own around 10 percent through ESOPs. Eternal Group CFO Akshant Goyal is the largest angel investor with nearly 4 percent.

What to Watch

Temple's next funding round will be the real market test. If it closes at or near the $500 million valuation that Goyal has flagged to employees, it would rank among the fastest early-stage valuation climbs in Indian startup history — a signal that global capital is betting big on longevity tech out of India. The startup's commercial launch timeline and the scientific community's reception of its underlying research will determine whether the valuation momentum holds.
